papers.title: Proof-or-Stop: Don't Trust the Agent, Trust the Evidence -- Loop Engineering for Verifiable Evidence-Gated Lifecycle Control
papers.claim: Lifecycle transitions are permitted only when fresh, tracked-source-state-bound, mechanically verifiable evidence satisfies the relevant gate.

hypothesis: A sealed passing receipt whose identity exactly matches the current obligation identity prevents false lifecycle promotion when a relevant verification input changes.
null_hypothesis: Exact identity binding either fails to distinguish stale evidence from current evidence or rejects an unchanged verification scope unpredictably.
independent_variable: Result-only acceptance in the control versus a sealed receipt whose source, verifier, arguments, configuration, runtime, lockfiles, and scope identity must exactly match the current obligation in the treatment.

variants.name: control
variants.description: A test-local baseline permits a lifecycle claim whenever a receipt reports pass, without comparing its identity to current obligation state.

variants.name: treatment
variants.description: A pure receipt reducer permits a lifecycle claim only when a sealed passing receipt exactly matches current obligation identity.

metrics.primary: false lifecycle promotions across the frozen deterministic trace corpus
secondary: stale receipt rejections by rule ID
metrics.acceptance_rule: The treatment must produce zero false lifecycle promotions, accept every fresh passing trace, reject every stale, missing, failed, and tampered trace with a stable rule ID, and reach byte-equivalent state on replay.

evaluator.rubric: Inspect every trace: a lifecycle claim is allowed only with an untampered passing receipt whose identity exactly equals the current obligation identity; stale, missing, and failed receipts are rejected.
